prompt.context: Skedasky Farms is involved in the process of making, selling, and distributing white wines. As of late, industry growth has stagnated. The CEO wants to increase revenue, and has enlisted you to help.
prompt.question: Come up with ideas to help the CEO increase revenue.

clarifying_info.q: Does Skedasky grow its own grapes?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, they grow all of their raw inputs (grapes).

clarifying_info.q: Where are their farms and facilities located?
clarifying_info.a: Their farms are in California, with some processing facilities on-site, and another large facility located nearby.

clarifying_info.q: How does Skedasky sell its wine?
clarifying_info.a: They sell to wine distributors, and also sell directly to some stores in the state.

clarifying_info.q: What types of wine do they sell?
clarifying_info.a: They sell a variety of grades, from cheaper boxed wine to premium bottles.
The industry is very fragmented, and Skedasky has a comparable domestic market share to the other major winemakers in its area.

framework: Current revenue streams: pricing strategy and volume growth
New revenue streams: new products and new business lines
Market expansion: geographic and channel diversification

questions.prompt: What are ideas to increase revenue from current operations?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure ideas across price and volume levers. Price: examine price elasticity by grade (boxed vs premium), by buyer type, by wine variety. Volume: increase shelf space, seek new distributors or stores, increase international exposure, rebrand the wine.

questions.prompt: Skedasky thinks they have a good case for beginning to make and sell beer. What are some possible reasons this could be a good idea?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify synergies: leverage the brand name and distribution channels; economies of scale in SG&A and other expenses; potential equipment sharing between wine and beer production.

questions.prompt: How may Skedasky want to enter the beer market and what are some associated concerns?
questions.guidance: Three entry modes: (1) Organic growth — pros: more control, no integration problems; cons: takes time, lengthy trial-and-error if lacking brewing expertise. (2) Acquisition — pros: facilities/resources ready to go, leverage target brand name; cons: integration issues (culture clash), potentially expensive. (3) Joint venture/Alliance — combines speed with partial control. Candidate should also raise financing concerns: depends on current leverage and available free cash.

questions.prompt: For a more immediate revenue impact, the client is considering changing the price of their mid-upper level bottles. Currently 10,000 bottles are sold per year at $20 each. A 10% price increase leads to a 10% volume decrease; a 10% price decrease leads to a 5% volume increase. Which course should the company take?
questions.guidance: Candidate must ask for profit margin before calculating. Margins are currently 50% of $20 (i.e., cost = $10). Compare profit under three scenarios: current, 10% price increase, 10% price decrease. Conclude that a 10% price increase is most favorable, yielding an ~8% profit increase.

math.setup: Current: Price=$20, Cost=$10, Margin=$10, Volume=10,000 → Profit=$100,000. Candidate must ask for margin (50% of $20).
steps: 10% Price Increase: Price=$22, Cost=$10, Margin=$12, Volume=9,000 → Profit=12×9,000=$108,000
10% Price Decrease: Price=$18, Cost=$10, Margin=$8, Volume=10,500 → Profit=8×10,500=$84,000
math.answer: 10% price increase yields $108,000 profit, an ~8% increase over the current $100,000. This is the recommended course.

brainstorming.prompt: Come up with ideas to increase revenue, both from current and new revenue streams.

categories.name: Current revenue — Price
ideas: Examine price elasticity by wine grade (boxed vs premium)
Segment pricing by buyer type (distributor vs direct retail)
Differentiate pricing by wine variety (Cabernet vs Merlot)

categories.name: Current revenue — Volume
ideas: Increase share of shelf space at existing retailers
Seek new distributors or new retail store accounts
Rebrand wine to attract new customer segments

categories.name: New revenue streams
ideas: Wine tours and private tastings for premium/wealthy buyers
Release new brands or varieties of top-selling wines
Expand into red and sparkling wines

recommendation: Enter the beer market via acquisition to leverage existing distribution and brand, while benefiting from the target's facilities and brand name
Immediately raise prices 10% on mid-upper range bottles, which research shows will increase profit in that category by approximately 8%
risks: Beer acquisition may face integration challenges (culture clash) and could be expensive
Brand may not carry over from wine to beer; management capabilities may not transfer
Price increase could accelerate long-term volume erosion if consumer preferences shift
next_steps: Conduct further research to identify and evaluate potential beer acquisition targets
Run similar price elasticity studies across all other product lines to find additional pricing opportunities
Explore international distribution channels to diversify geographic revenue
